Evidence: Unsolved murder, prosecutor ghosting, police cold case
#TrueCrime #Justice

Media and family narratives present a dedicated mother seeking justice and transparent accountability for her murdered daughter.

The Marion County Prosecutor's Office and IMPD have maintained complete silence, leaving a decade-old homicide investigation stalled in administrative limbo.

Christina Kramer's relentless advocacy ensures her daughter's memory and case remain alive despite a decade of bureaucratic abandonment.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The audit catches a severe Plane Error: confusing emotional media headlines with institutional accountability. The core failure lies in prosecutorial inaction.

Social Physics Analysis:
The prosecutor's office runs a Smart Selfish maneuver by ignoring public inquiries and stonewalling the family, maintaining institutional comfort over transparent justice while shifting the burden of grief entirely onto the victim's mother.

When public institutions abandon their duty to investigate violent crime, transparent ideals collapse into systemic neglect and destruction.

No mother should have to spend a decade begging strangers just to find out who stole her daughter's future. True healing requires truth and accountability.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Young woman joked about going missing — 10 years later, mom won't rest until she finds out who killed her

Angie Barlow vanished after texting her roommate about a private party gig in Indianapolis. Her mother says prosecutors have gone silent on the case.

Actual Article Body:
This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed. ©2026 FOX News Network, LLC. All rights reserved. Quotes displayed in real-time or delayed by at least 15 minutes. Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

Angie Barlow, 23, disappeared on Oct. 26, 2016, and her remains were found about eight months later in Indianapolis. She jokingly texted about going missing the night she vanished.

As an Indiana mother continues to search for answers in her daughter’s unsolved murder, she says it has been years without answers from Indianapolis prosecutors.

For Angie Barlow’s mother, Christina Kramer, the 10-year mark of her daughter’s disappearance brings questions about both her death and the status of the ongoing investigation.

Angie Barlow, 23, disappeared on Oct. 26, 2016, after texting her roommate the address of a private dancing gig at the Landmark Apartment and Townhomes in Indianapolis.

Angie Barlow, 23, disappeared on Oct. 26, 2016, in Indianapolis. Her remains were found nearly eight months later. (Courtesy of Christina Kramer)

GABBY PETITO'S MOTHER URGES PUBLIC 'RIPPLE EFFECT' TO HELP FIND THE MISSING 5 YEARS AFTER DAUGHTER'S MURDER

"About to work this private party in case I go missing LOL," the text message read, Kramer told Fox News Digital.

Nearly eight months later, searchers found Barlow’s remains in a backyard of a residence off Harcourt in Indianapolis, WISH-TV reported. Kramer said her daughter had been fatally shot.

TEEN FOUND IN SHALLOW CALIFORNIA VINEYARD GRAVE IDENTIFIED NEARLY 50 YEARS LATER AS FAMILY WARNS KILLER

Kramer added that she is desperate for answers after a special prosecutor assigned to the case left the office. She estimated it had been around two years since she has heard from the Marion County Prosecutor’s Office.

"I had been sending a bunch of emails for I don't even know how long to absolutely nobody," Kramer told Fox News Digital, adding that she no longer has a point of contact with the prosecutor’s office.

The Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department said the investigation into Angie Barlow's death remains open. (Courtesy of Christina Kramer)

JONBENET RAMSEY'S DAD PRESSES FOR NEW LAW IN DECADES-LONG HUNT FOR DAUGHTER’S KILLER

Kramer said she has also tried repeatedly to reach Marion County Prosecuting Attorney Ryan Mears but has not received a response.

The Marion County Prosecutor's Office did not respond to multiple requests for comment from Fox News Digital.

Kramer said surveillance footage from the apartment complex showed two vehicles leaving at around 3:30 a.m. on Oct. 27, 2016. She identified one vehicle as Barlow's blue Pontiac G6.

A black sedan followed closely behind, believed to have belonged to a female acquaintance who worked with Barlow at Club Rio in Indianapolis, Kramer said. The footage did not allow investigators to identify the drivers or occupants because of the vehicles' tinted windows, WISH-TV reported.

Kramer said days went by without answers. She then contacted the dealership where Barlow purchased the vehicle and used its GPS tracker to help locate it around eight miles from the apartment complex.

While Barlow normally kept her car meticulously clean, Kramer said the recovered vehicle had been completely trashed inside and looked as though it had been driven under a fence.

"That car had been on some kind of journey," Kramer added.

Kramer said months later, she received a phone call from the acquaintance who had been at the private party with her boyfriend. Kramer said that Barlow knew the pair, but they were not friends.

"She needed some quick cash, and this was the way to do it," Kramer said, adding that she would have never accepted the gig had she known who was there.

During the Jan. 2017 call, Kramer recalled asking the female acquaintance what she and Barlow had discussed at the party.

No charges have ever been filed in Angie Barlow's Indianapolis killing. (Mark E. Gibson via Getty Images)

"Oh, you want to know what her last words were," Kramer recalled the woman saying.

Kramer said the remark stayed with her because she interpreted it as a taunt. The woman denied making the call and having that conversation, according to what Kramer told Fox News Digital.

The Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department said that no criminal charges have been filed in Barlow’s death.

IMPD told Fox News Digital that the investigation remains open with Detective Jose Torres as the lead investigator but declined to comment further.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Despite standing less than 5 feet tall, Barlow excelled as a softball catcher, her mother said. She also competed in basketball, shot put, volleyball and bowling.

"She was a very gifted athlete. There was not a sport that she did not do," Kramer said. "Whenever I talk about her, especially the good things, it just, it makes you happy."

She was the eldest of four sisters, whom she remained close to after she left the family’s Muncie home.

"My daughter was the victim," Angie Barlow's mother, Christina Kramer, said. "She can't speak for herself. I'm her survivor. I'm her voice, and I speak for her." (Courtesy of Christina Kramer)

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Kramer said Barlow's death continues to affect the family, particularly her youngest daughter, who was 4 when Barlow disappeared.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

The youngest child turned to violent video games to learn "how to escape the bad people," Kramer said.

SEND US A TIP

Kramer said she will continue pressing authorities to solve her daughter's murder.

GOT A TIP?

"When you remain silent, you're a victim. When you have a voice, you're a survivor, and I refuse to be a victim of my circumstances," Kramer said.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"My daughter was the victim. She can't speak for herself. I'm her survivor. I'm her voice, and I speak for her."

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

The Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department urges anyone with information to contact its homicide office at 317-327-3475.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Tipsters can also contact Crime Stoppers of Central Indiana at 317-262-TIPS (8477), where callers can remain anonymous.

[Source 2 — nypost.com] (URL: https://nypost.com/2026/10/25/us-news/nyc-woman-sexually-assaulted-at-knifepoint-in-central-park-cops/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
NYC woman sexually assaulted at knifepoint in Central Park: cops

A woman was sexually assaulted near E 67th St in Central Park Saturday night, cops said.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A woman was sexually assaulted at knifepoint in Central Park Saturday night, according to the NYPD.

A brazen man approached a woman while brandishing a knife before sexually assaulting her inside the park near East 67th Street and Fifth Avenue around 8:30 p.m., cops said.

The woman was rushed to an area hospital where she is listed in stable condition.

The armed thug fled the scene wearing a black sweatshirt and pants with a black backpack, cops said.

Further information was not immediately available Saturday night.

Nearby residents were left shaken after hearing about the heinous assault.

“It’s very concerning for a very great area of New York City, and I’m uneasy with my fiancé walking her dog at night,” local resident Davis Defore told The Post.

Defore, 30, said he was just in Central Park walking his dog Harlow before the scene unfolded.

“I was like, ‘Oh, my goodness.’ It’s literally that same path. I let Harlow out in the field right there to go play,” he recalled.

Another local, 30-year-old Valentina Mizrahi, has lived in the neighborhood since 2021 and said she’s never been scared but her mother recently warned her not to walk alone at night “because it gets ugly” after having a conversation with a nearby hotel doorman.

No arrests have been made as of Saturday night.
